canonical.title: Count the number of nodes linked list

narrative.title: Counting Wagons in the Marshalling Yard
narrative.scenario: Yard control receives a consist whose cars are chained one-way with no manifest attached, so the only way to size the train is to walk it: step from car to car, tally as you go, and stop when the coupling leads nowhere. The final tally is the train's length.
narrative.inputFormat: An array arr representing the linked list's node values.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of nodes in the list.

testCases.explanation: The walk visits five cars before running off the end.
Seven nodes, so the tally stops at 7 — values play no role, only the count does.

hintLevels: Level 1: The values are irrelevant — length is purely how many hops the chain holds.
Level 2: Start a counter at zero, walk from the head, and increment once per node until the current pointer is null.
Level 3: A single-node list must return 1 and the loop condition (checking the node, not its next) is what makes the last node counted.
